Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) data from 1989, individuals with certain time preference behaviors, such as dissaving (DISSAVED) or stable savings (SAMESAVE), are associated with higher BMI. This relationship is suggested by the positive coefficients found in the linear regression analysis, although the statistical significance of these relationships could not be determined due to the absence of p-values. The correlation matrix also indicates weak positive relationships between BMI and these time preference variables, as well as with income and age.

WORKFLOW_SUMMARY:
1. Data Loading: Loaded the dataset from the specified path using Python.
2. Data Inspection: Displayed the first few rows of the dataset to understand its structure and the relevant columns.
3. Linear Regression Analysis: Performed a linear regression analysis using DISSAVED and SAMESAVE as predictor variables to determine their relationship with BMI.
4. Correlation Matrix Analysis: Calculated the correlation matrix to understand the relationships between BMI and other variables, including time preference indicators, after removing non-numeric columns.
